premise.usage: Node kind: a thesis that rests on nothing else. One or two words. Also used lowercased in the legend.
premise.note: Logic term: a claim the reasoning starts from. Not 'initial statement' in the sense of a first sentence.

conclusion.usage: Node kind: a thesis derived from others. One or two words. Also used lowercased in the legend.

restsOn.usage: Heading above the list of a thesis's premises. Up to three words, shown in capitals.

leadsTo.usage: Heading above the list of what follows from a thesis. Up to three words, shown in capitals.

derived.usage: Line above a conclusion's text; {refs} becomes a list of clickable numbers joined with the language's own 'and'.

noPremises.en: A starting claim: it rests on nothing else in the chain.
noPremises.usage: Shown instead of the premises list for a starting claim. One sentence.

noConsequences.en: A final conclusion: nothing follows from it.
noConsequences.usage: Shown instead of the consequences list for a final conclusion. One sentence.

prev.usage: Button: go to the previous thesis in reading order. Keep the arrow.

next.usage: Button: go to the next thesis in reading order. Keep the arrow.

collapse.usage: Button that collapses the side panel. One word.

expand.usage: Button that expands the collapsed side panel. One word.

fitAll.usage: Button that fits the whole graph on screen. Two words at most.

legendSelected.usage: Legend item for the selected node. Shown lowercased.

legendAncestors.usage: Legend item for nodes the selected one depends on, directly or indirectly. Shown lowercased.

legendDescendants.usage: Legend item for nodes that follow from the selected one. Shown lowercased.

hint.en: Drag or scroll to move the graph; Ctrl + scroll or + and − zoom. ← → go in order, ↑ to a premise, ↓ to a consequence, 0 shows the whole graph.
hint.usage: Help line at the bottom of the panel. Keep the key names as they appear on a keyboard.

graphLabel.en: Thesis graph: arrows lead from premises to conclusions
graphLabel.usage: Accessible label of the whole graph for screen readers.

nodeLabel.usage: Accessible label of a node for screen readers.

source.usage: Label before the link to the original article in the header. One word.

error.usage: Shown instead of the graph when the data is invalid. {message} is a technical English message.

views.usage: Accessible label of the tabs that switch between Summary, Audit and Logic. Pages with an analysis only.

viewSummary.usage: Tab: the bottom line of the analysis, with final conclusions, key points and key concepts. One word.

viewAudit.usage: Tab: the list of issues and the verdicts on starting claims. One word.

viewLogic.usage: Tab: the argument map. One word.

versions.usage: Accessible label of the switch between Original, Reconstructed and Optimized.

versionOriginal.usage: Switch option: the reasoning as the author gives it. One word.

versionReconstructed.usage: Switch option: the reasoning made explicit, with implicit premises and conditions added and fixes applied. One word.

versionOptimized.usage: Switch option: the reconstructed reasoning reduced to the fewest starting claims. One word.

reduction.usage: Counter next to the switch in the optimized version; each placeholder becomes 'before → after', e.g. '25 → 12'.

finalConclusions.usage: Summary heading: conclusions that nothing else follows from.

keyPoints.usage: Summary heading: the conclusions that carry the argument.

keyConcepts.usage: Summary heading: terms the reader needs to follow the argument.

senses.usage: Mark next to a term that the article uses in more than one sense; {count} is a number.

strength.usage: Label of a number from 0 to 1: how firmly a thesis is established. One word.
strength.note: The strength of an argument, not physical force.

weakestPool.usage: Fills {reason} in 'weakest' when the weakest link is a pool; {refs} becomes a list of thesis numbers.

weakest.usage: Line under a strength: what lowered it. {reason} is a reason from the analysis, in the article's language.

issues.usage: Heading of the list of problems found in the reasoning.

issueCount.usage: Counts under the Issues heading; the placeholders are numbers.

flaw.usage: Severity: the problem breaks the reasoning. One word.

weakness.usage: Severity: the reasoning holds, but less firmly than the article presents it. One or two words.

issueNonSequitur.usage: Issue type: a plain name first, the textbook name in parentheses.

issueMissingPremise.usage: Issue type: a plain name first, the textbook name in parentheses.

issueCircular.usage: Issue type: a plain name first, the textbook name in parentheses.

issueEquivocation.usage: Issue type: a plain name first, the textbook name in parentheses.

issueStrawMan.usage: Issue type: a plain name first, the textbook name in parentheses.

issueInconsistency.usage: Issue type: a plain name first, the textbook name in parentheses.

issueIrrelevantConclusion.usage: Issue type: a plain name first, the textbook name in parentheses.

concept.usage: What an issue is about when it concerns a term; {term} is the term.

wholeArgument.usage: What an issue is about when it concerns the argument as a whole.

fixedBy.usage: Under an issue; {refs} becomes the clickable numbers of the theses the fix added or changed.

noFix.en: No fix: the issue stays in the reconstructed logic.
noFix.usage: Under an issue that has no fix. One sentence.

startingClaims.usage: Heading of the list of verdicts on the claims the reasoning starts from.

claimCount.usage: Counts under the Starting claims heading; the placeholders are numbers.

verdict.usage: Panel label before a starting claim's verdict. One word.

verdictSupported.usage: Verdict: the backing covers what the claim says.

verdictWeak.usage: Verdict: some backing, but it falls short.

verdictFalse.usage: Verdict: contradicted by the article or a checked source.

verdictDefinition.usage: Verdict for a definition, which isn't rated.

step.usage: Panel label before a conclusion's reasoning type and step strength. One word.

typeDeductive.usage: Reasoning type: the conclusion follows necessarily.

typeGeneralization.usage: Reasoning type: from cases to a general claim.

typeAbductive.usage: Reasoning type: from an effect to the cause or action that best accounts for it.

typeAnalogy.usage: Reasoning type: what holds for one case holds for another.

condition.usage: Panel label: what a non-deductive step relies on without saying so.

ratingStrong.usage: Rating of an implicit condition, shown lowercase after the label.

ratingWeak.usage: Rating of an implicit condition, shown lowercase after the label.

ratingNone.usage: Rating of an implicit condition that doesn't hold, shown lowercase after the label.

pool.usage: Panel label: premises that are alternative evidence and count as one. One word.
pool.note: A pool of evidence, not a swimming pool.

added.usage: Mark on a thesis that the reconstructed logic added: an implicit premise the article relies on but doesn't state.

fixes.usage: Panel label before the issues whose fix added or changed the thesis. One word.

flawNoFix.en: A flaw with no fix sets this step to 0
flawNoFix.usage: Panel line on a conclusion broken by a flaw that has no fix.

glossary.meaning: A thesis that a conclusion follows from
A thesis with no premises: the reasoning starts from it
A claim derived from other claims
Any single claim in the graph, starting claim or conclusion
A claim that follows from the selected one
How firmly a thesis is established, a number from 0 to 1
Alternative pieces of evidence for one conclusion, counted together
